idiom_name: committed golden files under tests/ + a hand-written -u update mode over cmocka/Unity
implementation_notes: C ships neither a test framework nor snapshot support in its standard library - cmocka or Unity provide the runner and assertions only - so the characterization harness is assembled by hand: run the subject with each fixture input, capture stdout and any files it produces into a buffer, compare byte for byte against a committed reference under tests/golden/, and expose an update mode (-u on the test binary, or an environment variable) that rewrites the reference so the diff can be reviewed before it is committed. The classic hand-rolled form is the norm here and is perfectly adequate at small scale; a string/lines comparison function with a printed diff is the only piece of infrastructure worth writing carefully.
pitfalls: Byte comparison punishes irrelevant variation: timestamps, temporary paths, pointer values and locale-dependent formatting must be normalized (or masked by the capture) before comparing, or the suite flakes and gets ignored.
Raw struct dumps include padding and uninitialized bytes that differ between builds and runs; capture a canonical text or length-prefixed binary serialization instead.
The subject may call exit(), abort() or crash on some inputs: fork() the case (or install a signal guard) so one bad input fails one test instead of killing the run.
Missing reference files must fail the test, not be created silently: a 'write if absent' branch turns the first green CI run into an accidental recording.
